example_input: Summarize what we decided about the API rate limits yesterday
note: Representations below are simplified shapes of the real types at the pinned SHA, not verbatim dumps.

steps.narrative: The user sends 'Summarize what we decided about the API rate limits yesterday'. From the CLI, `hermes` parses the message through `fire.Fire(main)`; from Telegram, the gateway maps the inbound event to a `SessionSource` and derives a session key via `_session_key_for_source`, honoring per-user/thread/profile namespaces. Either way the message lands in `AIAgent.run_conversation`, which stamps the `{turn_id, current_turn_user_idx}` boundary on every envelope.
steps.title: Input
steps.representation:
hermes "Summarize what we decided about the API rate limits yesterday"
  CLI:      fire.Fire(main) -> AIAgent.run_conversation
  Telegram: inbound event -> SessionSource -> _session_key_for_source
            (per-user/thread/profile namespaces)
  -> envelope stamped {turn_id, current_turn_user_idx}

steps.narrative: Before the turn starts, the session turn lease is acquired — concurrent prompts against the same session serialize on the lease instead of interleaving. The lease holder is recorded so a crashed turn can be detected and the lease reaped.
steps.title: Lease
steps.representation:
acquire turn lease for session
  -> concurrent prompts serialize on the lease (no interleaving)
  -> lease holder recorded -> crashed turn detected, lease reaped

steps.narrative: Turn-start preflight runs before any model call: idle compaction and proactive compression shrink the context first, then budget and iteration state are checked. Overflow (context too big) and truncation (response cut mid-stream) are handled by two separate verdict machines later — but the turn starts by making room, not by hoping it fits.
steps.title: Preflight
steps.representation:
turn-start preflight (before any model call):
  -> idle compaction + proactive compression shrink context first
  -> check budget + iteration state
  # overflow vs truncation handled by separate verdict machines later

steps.narrative: The system prompt is byte-stable for the life of the conversation — the prompt-caching invariant. Nothing rebuilds it mid-turn; skill invocations and other injections ride user messages or tool results instead. Tool schemas come from `get_tool_definitions`, memoized and generation-keyed on the registry, with per-platform rewriters. When the tool catalog is large, the model sees only the Tool Search bridge (`tool_search` / `tool_describe` / `tool_call`) and the real schemas assemble on demand.
steps.title: Prompt assembly
steps.representation:
system prompt: byte-stable for the conversation lifetime
    # the prompt-caching invariant — never rebuilt mid-turn
  -> skill invocations / injections ride user messages or tool results
tools: get_tool_definitions (memoized, generation-keyed, per-platform rewriters)
  -> large catalog? model sees only tool_search / tool_describe / tool_call
     real schemas assemble on demand

steps.narrative: The in-turn loop runs `while (api_call_count < max_iterations and iteration_budget.remaining > 0) or budget_grace_call` — max_iterations defaults to 500. Each iteration calls the provider's transport (`chat_completions` by default; `codex_responses` for openai-codex, copilot, and friends) with the OpenAI-format message list. Reasoning content is stored in `assistant_msg['reasoning']`. Our question needs yesterday's context, so the model calls `session_search`.
steps.title: Model call
steps.representation:
while (api_call_count < max_iterations and iteration_budget.remaining > 0)
      or budget_grace_call            # max_iterations defaults to 500
  -> provider transport: chat_completions | codex_responses
  -> OpenAI-format message list; reasoning -> assistant_msg['reasoning']
  our turn: model calls session_search

steps.narrative: `handle_function_call` is the single dispatch funnel: Tool Search bridge unwrap, connector dispatch, request middleware, plugin `pre_tool_call` hooks, ACP edit approval — then `registry.dispatch`, then the `transform_tool_result` hook. Our `session_search` call hits the gateway approval queue first: without approval (or YOLO mode), the tool waits; the denial breaker counts refusals per session. Approved, it runs FTS5 over the message index — with the custom CJK bigram tokenizer — and returns yesterday's rate-limit discussion.
steps.title: Dispatch
steps.representation:
handle_function_call (single dispatch funnel):
  tool_search unwrap -> connector dispatch -> request middleware
  -> plugin pre_tool_call hooks -> ACP edit approval
  -> registry.dispatch -> transform_tool_result hook
session_search -> gateway approval queue first (or YOLO mode)
  -> approved: FTS5 over message index (custom CJK bigram tokenizer)
  -> returns yesterday's rate-limit discussion

steps.narrative: Between iterations, guardrails watch for identical-call loops and runaway tool use; the loop also checks the interrupt flag every iteration so the user can stop it mid-turn. The model gets the search results as a tool message and answers from them — no tool calls in the response, so the loop exits the API-call cycle.
steps.title: Answer
steps.representation:
between iterations:
  -> guardrails watch: identical-call loops, runaway tool use
  -> interrupt flag checked every iteration (user can stop mid-turn)
model gets tool message with search results -> answers from them
  -> no tool calls in response -> exit the API-call cycle

steps.narrative: The turn persists to SessionDB (SQLite/WAL) and then the learning loop kicks in: `_spawn_background_review` forks the agent in a daemon thread to replay the turn and ask 'should any skill/memory be saved or updated?' — writes go straight to the memory and skill stores without touching the prompt cache. Separately, when the agent sits idle past the curator interval (default 7 days), `maybe_run_curator` reviews skill lifecycles: pin, archive, consolidate — never delete.
steps.title: Learn
steps.representation:
turn -> SessionDB (SQLite/WAL)
_spawn_background_review (daemon thread):
  -> replay turn: "should any skill/memory be saved or updated?"
  -> writes go straight to memory/skill stores (prompt cache untouched)
idle past curator interval (default 7 days):
  -> maybe_run_curator: pin | archive | consolidate skills (never delete)
